scope: Exact current-donor source decomposition of the Realtime voice -> claude_frage delegated child policy envelope. No host/VPS/provider execution was performed.

atoms.what_it_does: gespraech.berechtigung defaults to acceptEdits and the setter explicitly accepts acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, auto and dontAsk. gespraech_status returns this value to the voice daemon.
atoms.reason: A mutable runtime permission-mode string is input to child execution policy; it must not itself become canonical authorization.

atoms.what_it_does: fuehren_gespraech constructs RealtimeSession with cfg.berechtigung (fallback acceptEdits), and _claude_taetigkeit forwards self._berechtigung to gespraechsmodus.claude_frage with timeout=600. It does not pass a cwd override in this path.
atoms.reason: The voice TaskAdmission and the effective child execution policy need an immutable binding across this bridge.

atoms.what_it_does: claude_frage constructs claude -p with --permission-mode <berechtigung>, hard-coded --disallowedTools Bash and --append-system-prompt. It supplies neither an explicit --settings argument nor an explicit settings artifact identity. If cwd is omitted, subprocess.run uses Path.home() as cwd.
atoms.reason: A Bash denial is useful but is not a complete deterministic policy envelope for all state-changing child capabilities, and historical --settings inheritance cannot be assumed to be the explicit policy source for this invocation.

atoms.what_it_does: frank_auftrag_stellen has a mechanical two-step confirmation predecessor before dispatch, but after dispatch the child process policy is separately determined by the permission/tool/cwd/settings surfaces above.
atoms.reason: Frankenstein 2.0 must preserve HumanIntentDecision as a distinct typed state rather than treating confirmation as a substitute for invocation-level effect authorization.

architecture_delta.purpose: Bind the exact delegated execution policy to TaskAdmission/workpackage and native child identity before any mutation/effect credit.
architecture_delta.execution_rule: A delegated child may receive candidate work after TaskAdmission, but mutation/effect credit requires observed effective policy identity plus invocation-bound one-shot EffectDecision/CapabilityLease at the actual side-effect boundary. ChildPolicyEnvelope cannot self-grant capabilities.
architecture_delta.historical_settings_rule: Historical --settings/wache-befehl inheritance remains donor evidence only. It may inform the successor design but is not silently credited to the current claude_frage invocation because this donor command does not explicitly pass --settings.
architecture_delta.bash_rule: Hard Bash denial remains a useful narrow guard. It must not be promoted to whole-child containment because non-Bash mutating tools and host-managed policy surfaces are separate capability classes.
architecture_delta.trigger4_handoff: Before Triggerword-4 R2/child freeze, bind workpackage/native-child identity and ChildPolicyEnvelope, then prove effective installed-host policy with harmless source-bound lifecycle/tool-hook evidence.

contradictions.a: Voice task dispatch has a mechanically evidenced two-step HumanIntent predecessor.
contradictions.b: The downstream child permission mode is independently configurable and may be bypassPermissions; the donor command only hard-denies Bash.

contradictions.a: Historical project evidence supports inherited --settings blocking in at least one helper-session lineage.
contradictions.b: Current donor claude_frage does not explicitly pass --settings or bind a settings artifact identity.

counterhypotheses.claim: The installed Claude Code host/global/managed settings may automatically inject an equivalent deterministic policy even without an explicit --settings CLI argument.
counterhypotheses.falsifier_or_discriminator: Observe the exact installed build plus effective settings/hook provenance for one harmless delegated child and bind lifecycle/tool-hook payloads to the workpackage and invocation.

counterhypotheses.claim: Hard --disallowedTools Bash plus the configured permission mode may be sufficient for the intended narrow voice-task capability envelope.
counterhypotheses.falsifier_or_discriminator: Enumerate every non-Bash mutating tool reachable in the installed child and test whether each reaches deterministic HumanIntent/Capability/Effect admission before mutation.

next_exact_gate: On an authorized installed-host surface only: capture one harmless voice-confirmed delegated child invocation and attest workpackage_id + native agent/task/tool identity + effective permission/settings/cwd policy. Then enumerate non-Bash mutating capability classes and prove each converges on an invocation-bound deterministic admission/effect boundary before Triggerword-4 child-runtime credit.
